english_translation: Forging iron required great craftsmanship, which was used to make spears.

dialogue.shona: Kugadzira masimbi kwaida hunyanzvi hukuru, hwaishandiswa kugadzira mapfumo.
dialogue.english: Forging iron required great craftsmanship, which was used to make spears.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Kugadzira [to / at gadzira] • masimbi [plural simbi] • kwaida [kwaida] • hunyanzvi [hunyanzvi] • hukuru [hukuru] • hwaishandiswa [hwaishandiswa] • kugadzira [to / at gadzira] • mapfumo [plural pfumo]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About How Things Used to Be: The '-ai-' Past Habitual ('hwaishandiswa')
grammar_notes.content: In this sentence, 'hwaishandiswa' uses the past habitual/imperfect marker '-ai-'. Whenever you talk about how people used to live in historical times, or an ongoing state in the past ('used to do', 'was/were doing'), Shona combines the subject prefix with '-ai-' + the verb stem: for example, 'vaigara' ('they used to live'), 'vaitengeserana' ('they used to trade with one another'), 'yaivakwa' ('it used to be built'), and 'hwaizivikanwa' ('it was renowned/known').
grammar_notes.rule: Subject Prefix + -ai- + Verb Stem = 'used to [verb] / was [verb]-ing' (va- + -ai- + -bva = vaibva, 'they came from')

grammar_notes.title: The Passive Voice ('-wa' / '-iwa') in 'hwaishandiswa'
grammar_notes.content: Notice how 'hwaishandiswa' ends in '-wa' right before the final '-a'. In Shona, you turn an active verb into a passive verb ('is done / was done')  simply by inserting '-w-' (or '-iw-' / '-ew-') before the final vowel '-a'! For example: '-bika' (cook) becomes '-bikwa' ('be cooked', as in 'pakubikwa'), '-vaka' (build) becomes '-vakwa' ('be built'), '-ruma' (bite/sting) becomes '-rumwa' ('be stung', as in 'arumwa nenyuchi'), and '-zivikanwa' means 'be known'.

grammar_notes.title: Infinitive Verbs & Action Nouns with 'ku-' ('Kugadzira')
grammar_notes.content: Look at 'Kugadzira' in this sentence. Every Shona verb in its dictionary ('to do') form begins with 'ku-': for example, 'kudya' (to eat), 'kutenga' (to buy), 'kubhadhara' (to pay), 'kuona' (to see), and 'kurwa' (to fight). Because 'ku-' verbs also behave as action nouns ('eating', 'paying', 'working'), you can attach linking prefixes directly to them: 'yekubhadhara' ('for paying'), 'pakubikwa' ('in the cooking'), and 'nekuona' ('by/with seeing').
grammar_notes.rule: ku- + Verb Stem = 'to [verb] / [verb]-ing' (ku- + -tenga = kutenga, 'to buy'; ye- + kubhadhara = yekubhadhara, 'for paying')

cultural_notes.title: Pre-Colonial Iron Smelting ('Kupfura Masimbi') & Master Blacksmiths
cultural_notes.content: Archaeological sites across Zimbabwe reveal clay blast furnaces ('mavruko') where master Shona blacksmiths ('mhizha dzekupfura simbi') smelted high-grade iron ore to forge agricultural hoes ('mapadza'), axes ('matemo'), and ceremonial spears ('mapfumo').
